classification.difficultyReason: Reading the period from the graph is direct. Reducing 500° by the period is a short step. Extending the asymptote pattern past the plotted domain requires a small unsignposted generalisation.

content.prompt: The graph of $y=\tan x$ is shown for $0^{\circ}\leq x\leq540^{\circ}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the graph to find the period of $y=\tan x$.

answer.worked:
The graph repeats between consecutive asymptotes, for example from $x=90^{\circ}$ to $x=270^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{period}&=270^{\circ}-90^{\circ}\\&=180^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the value of $x$ with $0^{\circ}\leq x<180^{\circ}$ for which $\tan x=\tan500^{\circ}$.

answer.worked:
The graph repeats every $180^{\circ}$, so subtract two periods.
$$\begin{align*}x&=500^{\circ}-2\times180^{\circ}\\x&=140^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: The graph is continued past $x=540^{\circ}$. Find the values of $x$ with $540^{\circ}<x<1000^{\circ}$ where it has vertical asymptotes.

answer.worked:
The last asymptote shown is at $x=450^{\circ}$, and they repeat every $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}450^{\circ}+180^{\circ}&=630^{\circ}\\630^{\circ}+180^{\circ}&=810^{\circ}\\810^{\circ}+180^{\circ}&=990^{\circ}\end{align*}$$The next one, $1170^{\circ}$, is beyond $1000^{\circ}$.
